eleven_substantial_dimensions.text: ## 1. Core thesis: cooperation needs two willing lives and usable information
## 2. Longitudinal states: local change without a fabricated conversion
## 3. Fuuka → Juri: recognition that sometimes carries a painful limit
## 4. Juri → Fuuka: help, wanted craft and protective mistakes
## 5. Ordinary ends: a kitchen is not the whole of either life

serious_rivals.text: **R1 — Complementary skills already make the pair reciprocal.** Useful preparation, Fuuka's indispensability statement and actual shared pancakes give this reading considerable force. It correctly refuses to measure Juri only by failed cooking. But operational need is not a full account of both wanted lives: Juri hears a painful identity limit, Fuuka still voices overload, and MINI reassurance lacks decisive information. The bounded reading is actual cooperation with uncompleted fairness and communication debts, not a relation devoid of reciprocity. [N03 L96–98; N04 L176]

**R2 — Fuuka alone is the competent caretaker.** Her repeated burden, practical knowledge and attempted prevention support the asymmetry. The reading fails if it erases Juri's competent service, contest/parfait, useful assistance, effective decoy and chosen identity, or removes Fuuka's own concealment proposal. The asymmetry is an important feature of particular work, not a warrant to make one girl all agency and the other only a problem. [N01 L518–520; N02 L104; N03 L70/89–98]

**R3 — Juri's affection and effort excuse her mistakes.** Trying to protect Fuuka's holiday, gratitude and repeated practice are meaningful, and Fuuka actually thanks the attempted care. Still, customer distress, Iori's experience and teacher fading are not canceled by intention. The relation needs recognition of effort together with an answer to what another must endure. Treating effort as worthless is unjustified; treating it as sufficient is also unjustified. [N03 L72–75/98; N02 L102–106; N06]

**R4 — Concealment prudently protects the club and its future.** Scarce resources and feared budget reduction make the temptation intelligible. The initial checklist praise and the harmed inspector's independent situation nonetheless remain; preserving the club cannot be treated as permission to remove a relevant victim from view. No completed concealment is printed, so neither accomplished wrongdoing nor successful protection is available as an ending. Fuuka's good work and bad proposal coexist locally. [N02 L88–106]

**R5 — Comedy makes the harm harmless.** Surreal food, genre flags, theatrical reactions and resumed routine allow a light tonal reading. They do not erase the frightened customers, unwelcome restraint, victim protest, lost rest or Juri's distress. The text can end an incident without completing a clinical or reparative audit. Acknowledging comic form is stronger when it retains the adverse written acts than when it silently translates them into assent. [N03 L75–94; N04 L170/176]

**R6 — The story is a steady maturation into safe equal cooking.** Continued practice and the final shared meal are unusually strong positive evidence. That local learning must survive. Yet source-world chronology is unanchored across classes, the private final soup remains unresolved and the event's workload complaint persists. A particular successful offer and meal support responsive accomplishment; they do not certify permanent mastery, a variant ladder or a finished labor arrangement. [N01 L520/546–550; N03 L96–98]

**R7 — Good food simply is effective care.** Taste, warmth, cute craft and sincere affection make shared food more than a safety problem. But quantity discomfort, varied household preference, dangerous hospitality and explicit refusal permission distinguish pleasure, safety, permission and benefit. Izumi's enjoyed juice and Iori's adverse response must both remain. The responsive relationship asks which recipient enjoys or accepts which offer, not whether food as an abstract category is benevolent. [N01 L518; N02 L102–106; N03 L96–98; N04 L174]

**R8 — Fuuka's protection suppresses Juri's chosen self.** Juri's hurt at the noncombatant implication and Fuuka's anxiety provide a serious basis for this reading. Actual support for the chosen café shift, indispensable help and accepted final offer are equally strong contrary evidence. The dyad contains tension between recognition of present usefulness and the identity the maker wants; it is not adequately described as either total domination or perfectly successful encouragement. [N03 L68/96–98]

**R9 — The pair is only an institutional arrangement.** Shared work, resources and inspection criteria explain recurrence and burden. They do not exhaust wanted company, care for another's holiday, gratitude, hurt recognition and trust in a call. Conversely, affective warmth cannot substitute for institutional repair. The separate home boundary is an interpretive necessity: this directed argument follows what each person can answer, while the institution must independently account for the resources and evaluation that shape those answers. [N02 L88; N03; N04; original GEHENNA responsibility4]

source_claim_join_receipts.literal_paragraph: Fuuka and Juri's relationship is neither a completed equal partnership nor a one-directional story of a competent caretaker carrying a useless dependent. They repeatedly help one another, take another's wanted life seriously and produce real shared good. Yet useful contribution, sincere reassurance and affection can coexist with unequal labor, incorrect explanations and information that a recipient needs but does not receive. Their most persuasive positive achievement is therefore particular responsive cooperation: Juri helps a worried Fuuka; Fuuka supports Juri's chosen service and thanks her attempt to protect a holiday; later Juri offers food with refusal expressly allowed, and Fuuka accepts. The actual shared eating matters. It does not silently settle permanent workload, safe future cooking or every past cost. [N02; N03]

source_claim_join_receipts.literal_paragraph: The relationship's ethical question is practical and literary: can the other person answer the actual request, knowing what it entails, while keeping a life and purposes of her own? Being pleased by food, being needed by a club and consenting to supply labor are different judgments. MINI's closing telephone reassurance makes that distinction unusually sharp. Juri trusts an account called protection while Fuuka is actually restrained and protesting. Juri's trust is real; informed approval of that restraint is not. The distorted account is external to the pair, but it acts on their communication and the work each expects of the other. Food and concern cannot replace the missing information. [N04 §8, `BA:mini:70006020:scene:003:u:0064–0079`]

source_claim_join_receipts.literal_paragraph: This does not make every scene an exercise in consent failure. Their independent repertoire resists an interpretation that values each girl only for how efficiently she keeps the kitchen or the other girl functioning. The dyad is compelling because two differentiated wanted lives meet inside a real working relation. [N01 L518–520; F01–F11; J01–J10]

source_claim_join_receipts.literal_paragraph: The represented episodes contain secure local sequences but no certified world calendar joining every BOND, whole message, group, gift, variant and event. The inspection has a three-hours-before-service opening and direct continuation into a revised grade. EVENT844 has a wanted day off, a café shift, an accident, a coordinated response and an explicit days-later kitchen coda.
